system.name: Cocoon-Emb
system.one_liner: Cocoon's optimization for embedding tables that pre-computes and coalesces correlated noise ahead of training to remove the per-iteration CPU-GEMV bottleneck

components.name: Baseline (CPU-GEMV)
components.role: reference timeline where each training iteration waits on a CPU GEMV noise computation

components.name: GPU Train
components.role: GPU training step per iteration in the baseline timeline

components.name: CPU GEMV
components.role: CPU noise-generation step per iteration in the baseline, performing the GEMV that dominates iteration time

components.name: Cocoon-Emb
components.role: optimized timeline that pre-computes noise ahead of training instead of per iteration

components.name: Hot/Cold Splitting
components.role: step 1: splits embedding-table entries by access frequency into hot or cold

components.name: Accelerated Pre-computation
components.role: step 2: pre-computes all correlated noises for the cold entries' future iterations before training starts

components.name: Noise Coalescing
components.role: step 3: coalesces and stores the pre-computed noises in a compact format

components.name: Noise Addition
components.role: step 4: adds the coalesced, pre-computed noise into each training iteration

components.name: Training
components.role: GPU training iterations (Iter 1, Iter 2, ..., Iter n) that run using the pre-computed noise

components.name: Speedup
components.role: annotated reduction in total timeline length achieved by Cocoon-Emb versus the baseline

content.key_idea: Instead of performing a per-iteration CPU GEMV that dominates training time, Cocoon-Emb splits table entries into hot/cold, pre-computes and coalesces noise for cold entries on the idle GPU before training starts, and adds it during training, yielding a large speedup.
content.reading_order: Top panel first (Baseline CPU-GEMV timeline, iteration by iteration), then bottom panel (Cocoon-Emb timeline) read left to right through the four circled steps, ending at the red Speedup bracket.

sections: \sysdlrm: Pre-computing and Storing Coalesced Noises for Embedding Tables
evidence: splits the table entries by access frequency into either hot or cold
efficiently pre-computes all the correlated noises to be used for the cold entries
pre-computing can use the faster GPU for GEMV, which idles before the training starts

summary: This figure compares two timelines for training embedding models under differentially private training. The top panel, 'Baseline (CPU-GEMV)', shows each GPU training iteration blocked on a much longer CPU GEMV noise-generation step, repeated every iteration. The bottom panel, 'Cocoon-Emb', shows the paper's optimization: circled steps 1-4 label hot/cold splitting of table entries by access frequency, accelerated pre-computation of correlated noise for cold entries on the otherwise-idle GPU before training starts, coalescing that noise into a compact stored format, and adding it into the actual training iterations. Because pre-computation reuses the same amount of GEMV work as the baseline but runs on a faster, otherwise-idle GPU with better data reuse, the training iterations run back-to-back, and a red 'Speedup' bracket on the right visualizes the resulting reduction in total timeline length. The figure is drawn as two stacked dashed-bordered horizontal timeline panels with gray/teal flat blocks, dotted iteration separators, and curved arrows connecting baseline iterations to their corresponding pre-computed blocks below.
summary_zh: 该图对比了差分隐私嵌入训练的两种时间线：上方基线中每次 GPU 训练迭代都要等待较长的 CPU GEMV 噪声计算；下方 Cocoon-Emb 通过冷热拆分、利用空闲 GPU 提前预计算、噪声合并与噪声添加四步，将噪声开销移出训练主循环，右侧红色括号标示由此获得的加速效果。
